# Brighton & Hove Food Partnership

The Brighton & Hove Food Partnership is a non-profit organization working towards a healthy, sustainable, fair food system for Brighton and Hove. The partnership has relationships with various entities, including the Council, Community and Voluntary Sector, Food SOS Campaign, Helen Starr-Keddle, Household Support Fund, Housing Department, and In the Bag Project.

## Key Partnerships

The Brighton & Hove Food Partnership has established partnerships with various organizations, including the Council, Community and Voluntary Sector, and Food SOS Campaign. These partnerships demonstrate the partnership's commitment to addressing food poverty and promoting a healthy food system. The relationships between these entities suggest that the partnership is well-positioned to leverage resources and expertise to achieve its goals.

## Helen Starr-Keddle's Role

Helen Starr-Keddle is a policy consultant for the Council advising on food poverty, and works one day a week as part of the food partnership. Her role highlights the importance of policy expertise in addressing food poverty and suggests that the partnership is well-positioned to influence policy decisions at the local level.

## In the Bag Project

The In the Bag project is a successful initiative funded by the local cricket club, which consists of ingredients and easy recipes packed into a bag that are distributed through food banks and affordable food projects. The partnership's involvement in this project suggests that it is committed to addressing food poverty and promoting food security, particularly among vulnerable populations.

## Household Support Fund

The Household Support Fund is a program that provides financial support to residents in need, and is used by the Council to prioritize spending. The partnership's relationship with this fund suggests that it is working to address food poverty and promote economic stability among vulnerable populations.

## Food SOS Campaign

The Food SOS campaign is an initiative to help address the shortage of surplus food, encouraging families to donate food to schools and businesses. The partnership's involvement in this campaign suggests that it is committed to promoting a healthy food system and reducing food waste.

## Community and Voluntary Sector

The Community and Voluntary Sector (CVS) organizations are composed of various entities, including the Brighton & Hove Food Partnership. The partnership's relationship with CVS suggests that it is working to leverage resources and expertise from the sector to address food poverty and promote a healthy food system.

## Council's Role

The Council works with the Brighton & Hove Food Partnership to prioritize spending of the Household Support Fund following a cash first approach. The partnership's relationship with the Council suggests that it is working to address food poverty and promote economic stability among vulnerable populations.

## Housing Department

The Housing Department works with the Brighton & Hove Food Partnership to address issues raised by the Emergency Food Network. The partnership's relationship with this department suggests that it is working to address housing-related issues and promote food security among vulnerable populations.

## Policy Expertise

The Brighton & Hove Food Partnership has established partnerships with various organizations, including the Council and Community and Voluntary Sector. These partnerships demonstrate the partnership's commitment to addressing food poverty and promoting a healthy food system through policy expertise.
